name: How does boat and RV storage construction differ from standard mini-storage?

mainEntity.name: How does boat and RV storage construction differ from standard mini-storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Adding boat and RV storage requires wider drive aisles, taller clear heights, and heavier-duty pavement compared to standard mini-storage. Standard drive aisles are typically 25 to 30 feet wide, but RV turning radiuses require 40 to 50 feet between buildings. Enclosed RV bays often need 14-foot-high overhead doors and lengths up to 45 to 50 feet. Slabs and asphalt sections must be engineered with thicker cross-sections and subbase reinforcement to support heavy axle loads without cracking or rutting.
